reason: I'd install it once because it's free and handles more file types, but my screenshots and PNGs open fine in Photos. I wouldn't go through the Windows Settings steps to make it default for that.
why_switch_or_not: The 26-of-32 formats claim is what gets me to try it. But my work is PNG screenshots and phone photos, and Photos already opens those. Speed is nice, but I haven't noticed Photos being slow enough to care. A one-developer 0.4.1 with an English-only UI, and having to tick formats and press Set default myself, makes me expect to forget about it after a few days.
current_app_pros: It's already there and opens when I double-click. It handles PNG, JPG, screenshots and phone photos without any setup. I don't have to think about it.
current_app_pains: It's a bit slow to start sometimes and flipping through hundreds of screenshots can lag. It's not a big deal though, and it can't open a few odd formats like AVIF or PSD, but I rarely get those.
objection: Another image viewer? Mine already works fine for screenshots and PNGs, and I'd have to set the default myself to make it stick.
would_change_my_mind: If I started getting AVIF, WebP, PSD or RAW files from work that Photos can't open, I'd make it the default straight away.
